explanation: 该论文研究北极变暖对植被生产力的影响，并使用地球系统模型来描述气候变率和变化如何影响北极生长积温，这与大气环境遥感技术中的气候变化监测和生态系统分析相关。
topic_words: ['Arctic greening', 'climate variability', 'Community Earth System Model 2', 'growing degree days', 'aerosol emissions']
authors: Daniel M Hueholt;Elizabeth A Barnes;James W Hurrell;Danica Lombardozzi;Ariel L Morrison
title: Exploring the influence of internal climate variability and forced change on Arctic greening
abstract: Warming Arctic temperatures are increasing terrestrial ecosystem productivity and allowing plant species to advance poleward. This Arctic greening has extensively altered regional ecosystems and climate, and it is projected to be a central element of future Arctic change. Existing fieldwork has identified increases in growing degree days (the annual sum of daily temperatures above 5 C) as a key driver of Arctic greening. We use the Community Earth System Model 2 Large Ensemble to describe how climate variability and change affect Arctic growing degree days over historical and future periods. We find that many simulated Arctic ecoregions have already entered a state in which the warming trend dominates over internal variability. Storylines of cases where this crossover occurs earlier or later allow us to connect these events to coupled climate variability. For the Brooks Range–a region where recent observations illustrate the treeline is rapidly advancing–we show that crossover in this region is associated with Pacific and Arctic sea surface temperature variability. Crossover into no-analog climate states relative to a preindustrial simulation begins in the mid-21st century around the circumpolar region. Mechanistic insights into the influence of coupled climate variability are robust to biases in the simulated high-latitude climate that stem from uncertainties in aerosol emissions. The methods we demonstrate provide a framework to incorporate contributions from internal variability and climate change together in future projections of ecosystem impacts.

explanation: 该论文研究了干旱适应与野火风险之间的权衡，重点关注了农田损失和城市化对西部美国的影响。虽然论文主要关注干旱和野火风险，但其中涉及了植被类型（如农田、草本植物、灌木）的燃烧特性分析，这与大气环境遥感技术中的植被监测和野火风险评估密切相关。因此，该论文与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）有较强的关联性。
authors: Austen A Lorenz;Beatrice L Gordon;Gabrielle F S Boisrame;Julia Berkey;Chelsea Cough;Rosemary W H Carroll;Christine M Albano
title: Out of the frying pan, into the fire? Tradeoffs between drought adaptation and wildfire risk under cropland loss and urbanization in the western United States
abstract: The western United States faces two escalating, co-occurring hazards in the form of persistent water scarcity (drought) and increasingly frequent wildfires in places humans live and recreate. Drought adaptation has emphasized water savings from cropland retirement, while wildfire adaptation has emphasized the fire risks of urbanization. By overlooking what retired cropland becomes and what development replaces, neither has fully examined cropland’s role as a landscape-scale buffer to wildfire in the western US. We demonstrate this buffering capacity across 11 states and 39 years of data, showing that cropland is less likely to burn than other vegetation classes. Within 477 watersheds where cropland has interacted with wildfire in the western US, approximately 4.29 million hectares of cropland was lost between 1985 and 2024. Cropland loss in most watersheds (77%) was consistent with fallowing transitions to more burnable herbaceous and scrubland vegetation across the Pacific Northwest, Inland Northwest, Intermountain West, and Great Basin. In a smaller portion of watersheds (19%), losses occurred through cropland-to-developed transitions clustered around major metropolitan areas in California, Idaho, Oregon, Washington, Utah, and Colorado, where development simultaneously removes buffering capacity and adds ignition sources. The remaining watersheds saw cropland transitions to wetlands and forests. Results highlight emerging tradeoffs between drought adaptation and wildfire risk in the western US, with retirement-driven fallowing and development-driven conversion reshaping where wildfires stop at landscape-scales. Integrated planning tools that evaluate water use savings and wildfire risks jointly, and expanded agricultural conservation programs that incorporate fire-buffering value, can help manage tradeoffs.

explanation: 该论文研究了西太平洋热带气旋活动在多种二氧化碳清除情景下的滞后响应，涉及气候模型、动力学机制和海表面温度变化，这与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测、大气成分分析和气旋活动监测密切相关。
topic_words: ['tropical cyclone', 'carbon dioxide removal', 'Genesis Potential Index', 'El Niño–like sea surface temperature hysteresis', 'vertical wind shear']
authors: Han-Kyoung Kim;Jong-Yeon Park;Doo-Sun R Park;Jae-Heung Park;Mincheol Moon
title: Hysteresis of western North Pacific tropical cyclone activity under multiple CO2 removal scenarios
abstract: Tropical cyclone (TC) activity is expected to change under future climate mitigation pathways, yet its response to carbon dioxide removal (CDR) remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the hysteretic response of the genesis potential index (GPI) over the western North Pacific (WNP) using an Earth system model under four idealized CDR scenarios with different peak CO2 concentrations. Although the WNP-mean GPI exhibits no significant hysteresis between the ramp-down and ramp-up periods at comparable CO2 concentrations across all scenarios, the underlying dynamical mechanisms fundamentally differ depending on the forcing magnitude. In the highest-to-moderate forcing scenarios, this lack of basin-mean hysteresis arises from a robust spatial compensation between a suppressed western WNP and an enhanced eastern WNP, forming a west-east dipolar pattern. This pattern is driven by an El Niño–like sea surface temperature hysteresis, which weakens the Walker circulation and alters vertical wind shear in opposite directions across the basin. Conversely, under the lowest forcing scenario, the absence of hysteresis is due to a negligible GPI response, as the El Niño–like warming remains too weak to trigger such dynamical chains. Our findings suggest a transition in the regional GPI response between the lowest and moderate forcing scenarios, indicating a nonlinear dependence of the regional TC genesis environment during CDR on the magnitude of the CO2 overshoot.

explanation: 该论文使用卫星和地面NO2测量数据，结合TROPOMI卫星传感器和GEOS-Chem模型，研究COVID-19疫情对中美欧三个人工NOx排放的影响。这直接涉及大气环境遥感技术和空气质量监测，因此与主题高度相关。
authors: Chongyuan Wu;Xiaoye Zhang;Lifeng Guo;Junting Zhong;Deying Wang;Jiaying Li;Bingyi Wu;Changhong Miao
title: COVID-19 impacts on anthropogenic NOx emissions in China, the contiguous U.S., and Europe: insights from joint TROPOMI and surface NO2 data assimilation
abstract: This study integrates satellite and surface NO2 measurements through the ensemble square root filter and the GEOS‐Chem model to estimate anthropogenic NOx emissions for China, the contiguous U.S., and Europe over 2019–2020, and further examines how the COVID‐19 pandemic altered emission patterns and sectoral contributions. Our results show that in 2020, anthropogenic NOx emissions were 19.20 ± 5.87 Tg in China, 8.96 ± 2.90 Tg in the contiguous U.S., and 10.56 ± 2.95 Tg in Europe. Compared with 2019, emissions decreased by about 5.38% in China, 8.94% in the contiguous U.S., and 15.38% in Europe. In China, emission reductions came from transportation, power plants, and industry. In contrast, reductions in the contiguous U.S. and Europe were almost entirely from transportation. These differences reflect the fundamental gap in energy structure and industry models between developed and developing economies. During the first wave of the pandemic, emissions fell sharply compared to the same period in 2019. The decreases were 18.04% in China, 10.56% in the contiguous U.S., and 21.74% in Europe. Large spatial variations were observed within each region. This work provides observation-based evidence of NOx emission changes across major world regions during COVID 19. It highlights how emissions can behave differently under sudden public health crises. The findings are useful for checking bottom-up emission inventories, assessing extreme events’ impacts on air quality, and designing better emission reduction policies.

explanation: 该论文主要关注的是盐碱化灌溉对小麦产量的影响以及区域特定的最佳灌溉阈值和风险，虽然涉及环境监测和数据分析，但并未明确提及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶反演等。
authors: Yimin Fang;Guoyong Leng;Linfei Yu;Jiali Qiu;Xiaoyong Liao
title: Global meta-analysis and machine learning uncover region-specific salinity thresholds and risks for sustainable wheat production under saline irrigation
abstract: Saline irrigation represents a pivotal alternative strategy for enhancing crop production under freshwater scarcity. However, previous assessments have mainly quantified average yield responses, while how interacting environmental and management conditions shape region-specific irrigation-water salinity thresholds and associated spatial risks remain elusive across global major breadbaskets. This study combined a meta-analysis of 551 field observations with machine learning (ML) to quantify global wheat yield responses to saline irrigation, identify optimal region-specific thresholds, and evaluate spatial risks in four major wheat-producing areas: the North China Plain (NCP), Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP), Middle East (ME), and Central California Valley (CCV). Meta-analysis revealed that saline irrigation led to significant average yield reductions ranging from 12.4% in the NCP to 31.4% in the CCV. ML further showed that irrigation water salinity, growing-season temperature, and irrigation amount emerged as the dominant drivers, collectively explaining more than 54% of yield variation. An optimum irrigation amount of 500 mm was optimal for maximizing yield under saline conditions. Region-specific best practices included border irrigation at flowering (FL) and grain-filling stages for the NCP, drip irrigation at these stages for the IGP, and drip irrigation at the FL stage for the ME and CCV. Spatial risk assessment revealed a mismatch between salinity tolerance thresholds and actual exposure. Under a conservative 5% yield-loss scenario, the IGP exhibited the highest model-derived salinity threshold of 4.14 dS m−1 but the largest risk area proportion due to elevated background salinity, whereas the ME faced the lowest risk, with a risk area of 7.7%, indicating high potential for saline water utilization. These findings highlight the limitations of universal water quality guidelines and demonstrate the necessity of localized management. By establishing a data-driven framework, this study provides actionable insights to safeguard global wheat supply, build climate resilience, and ensure agricultural sustainability in salt-affected environments.

explanation: 该论文研究了纳米布沙漠地区平流雾云底高度受大尺度气象过程的影响，涉及了大气层中的云层、边界层和雾的观测与分析，这些都与大气环境遥感技术（如云层监测、边界层分析）密切相关。
authors: Viola Hipler;Hendrik Andersen;Robert Spirig;Roland Vogt;Stuart Piketh;Bianca Adler;Jan Cermak
title: Synoptic and regional-scale meteorological controls of stratus altitude in the Namib Desert
abstract:
Fog is a key component of the Namib Desert ecosystem, and is mostly associated with the advection of marine stratus clouds. Here, we use local measurements near the coast to distinguish fog situations from lifted low-cloud situations. Using reanalysis data, we find synoptic and regional-scale processes over the ocean and over the continent that are connected to stratus altitude and therefore fog occurrence patterns. The results lead to a better understanding of the coastal desert fog system. 
 In the Namib Desert, fog is an essential water source and occurs when and where advected marine stratus clouds intersect with the land surface. However, the meteorological controls of the cloud base height are still insufficiently understood. This study aims to develop a basic understanding of the processes that influence the stratus altitude and, by extension, the spatial occurrence of fog. We combine satellite and in situ observations with large-scale meteorological data from reanalysis data (ERA5) to compare fog events to lifted stratus at the coast (low-cloud events). In fog situations, the marine boundary layer is shallower by up to 130 m along the entire coastline than in low-cloud situations. This is found to be related to the large-scale high-pressure systems. Fog situations exhibit a weaker Atlantic High but elevated continental pressure. The weaker Atlantic High is connected to less pronounced near-surface winds along the coastline, less cold advection, and heat fluxes upstream of the study region, leading to the shallower marine boundary layer. In parallel, higher continental pressures on fog days facilitate the formation of stronger nocturnal katabatic winds which can mix with, undercut or block the advected cloudy marine air. An alternative mechanism is highlighted in a case study of an off-season fog event, where a ridging high produces hot and dry subsiding easterly air masses which lower and intensify the inversion from above. To assess the predictive power of the continental and Atlantic high-pressure systems and the regional pressure pattern, a logistic regression is trained with three corresponding features. The classification outperformed a climatological baseline by ≈10 %, suggesting that the features contain relevant process information. The results improve our understanding of the processes that determine the seasonal and day-to-day variability of fog versus elevated low-cloud occurrence in the Namib.

explanation: 该论文研究了在低风速条件下尘埃的沉降动力学，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和大气成分分析密切相关。研究结果表明，尘埃的沉降速率在低风速下并非单调变化，而是存在一个最优风速，这对于改进大气模型中的尘埃去除和表征具有重要意义。
authors: Ruochen Jia;Chaoqun Ba;Chao Zhang;Wennong Kuang;Yuan Liu;Zhigang Wang;Fang Liu;Zhiming Xin;Yuting Liu;Qun Ma;Lu Zong;Wei Liang;Jianqiang Qian;Zhimin Liu
title: Non-monotonic response of net dust deposition  kinetics to low wind speeds
abstract:
Controlled wind tunnel experiments show how mineral dust settles under calm and low-wind conditions. Dust did not settle more slowly as wind speed increased. Instead, fine and medium-sized particles accumulated most strongly at a gentle wind speed of 2 m s−1, while stronger winds reduced their retention. These findings can help improve predictions of how dust is removed from the air and represented in atmospheric models. 
 Dry deposition is a major sink for mineral dust, yet its behavior under weak winds remains poorly constrained and is often parameterized monotonically with wind speed. Here we quantify size-resolved dust net accumulation kinetics in a closed-circuit recirculating wind tunnel using a two-stage protocol (brief high-wind loading followed by low-wind deposition at 0, 2, 4, and 6 m s−1). Cumulative retained-mass time series were measured with an array of collection trays, with the initial suspended dust loading recorded by an online concentration monitor. Particle sizes were characterized by laser diffraction and grouped into six diameter-threshold classes (PM2.5–PM63). A first-order kinetic model described the temporal accumulation dynamics and yielded a fitted asymptotic retained mass (a), effective net-accumulation rate coefficient (k), characteristic time scale (τ=1/k), and initial net accumulation flux (J0=ak). The observed J0 was highest at 2 m s−1 for PM2.5–PM30, and 4 m s−1 for PM40 and PM63, while J0 declined markedly at 6 m s−1 for the lower diameter thresholds. Quadratic fits across the four wind-speed levels suggest a potential maximum near 2–3 m s−1 for PM2.5–PM40. These measurements quantify the size-dependent response of effective surface retention to low wind speeds and provide benchmark behavior for coupled deposition, retention, and re-entrainment parameterizations.

explanation: 该论文研究 Fairbanks, Alaska 地区冬季表面逆温层中污染物（如 SO2 和 NO2）的垂直分布，使用差分光学吸收光谱技术进行观测，并与化学传输模型进行对比。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为差分光学吸收光谱是一种用于大气成分遥感的重要技术，主要用于监测和量化大气中的污染物浓度。
authors: Jochen Stutz;Jonas Kuhn;Sol Cooperdock;Sarah Johnson;Fangzhou Guo;James H. Flynn;Meeta Cesler-Maloney;William R. Simpson
title: Vertical distribution of pollution trapped by wintertime surface inversions in Fairbanks, Alaska, during the ALPACA experiment
abstract:
Northern cities often experience periods of wintertime air pollution, which are associated with surface temperature inversions and weak winds. In Fairbanks, Alaska, pollutants accumulate in a 20–40 m high surface layer with SO2 and NO2 mixing ratios of up to 35 and 65 ppb, respectively. This surface pollution is caused by the balance of emissions, chemistry, and inefficient mixing with clean background air. This balance has to be considered for air pollution mitigation strategies. 
 Air pollution in cold wintertime urban areas is a ubiquitous problem. Surface temperature inversions under low wind conditions and surface emissions lead to the formation of a shallow polluted surface layer (PSL). The presence of this PSL is well documented, but its height, the rates of exchange with the background atmosphere, and the interplay between vertical mixing and chemistry remain poorly quantified. Here we provide quantitative insights into this coupled chemistry-transport system using observations and modeling of vertical pollutant profiles.Long-path Differential Optical Absorption Spectroscopy of vertical trace gas profiles during the 2022 Alaskan Layered Pollution and Chemical Analysis (ALPACA) experiment in Fairbanks, Alaska, quantitatively track the frequent establishment of PSLs with heights of 20–40 m, which sometimes persist for several days. PSL trace gas mixing ratios often plateau at levels of up to 35 ppb SO2, 60 ppb NO2, 2.5 ppb HONO, 7 ppb HCHO, and low ozone as a result of surface emissions, gas-phase chemistry, and ineffective mixing with the background atmosphere. Parameterizing vertical mixing with observed surface temperature gradients and wind speed in the PACT-1D chemistry and transport model leads to excellent agreement of modeled and measured trace gas profiles. The PACT-1D transport scheme determines the residence time of pollutants within the PSL to be 1–4 h, confirming the strong influence of atmospheric mixing on the composition of sustained PSL events. Altitude-dependent ozone and NOx chemistry highlight the strong coupling between mixing and chemistry, which must be considered to quantify pollutant concentrations accurately in shallow PSLs.

explanation: 该论文使用Ka波段云雷达网络研究了中国云的垂直结构，涉及云层分布、高度、季节和地域变化，以及热力学、动力学和地表控制因素。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，特别是空气质量监测和大气成分分析。
topic_words: ['Ka-band cloud radar', 'atmospheric composition', 'aerosol retrieval', 'cloud vertical structure', 'air quality monitoring']
authors: Hui Xu;Jianping Guo;Jianbo Deng;Rongfang Yang;Deli Meng;Zhen Zhang;Ning Li;Yuping Sun;Shuairu Jiang;Tianmeng Chen;Juan Chen;Liping Zeng;Yongshui Zhou;Bing Tong
title: Cloud vertical structure across China from a national Ka-band cloud radar network: thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls
abstract:
Using a new national network of 80 cloud radars, we mapped how clouds are layered and how high they reach across China. Clouds vary strongly by region, season, and time of day, with deeper clouds in humid conditions and shallower clouds under stable or strong shear conditions. Afternoon single‑layer low CBH is significantly higher than all‑hour, especially over evergreen broadleaf. These findings help improve weather and climate predictions. 
 Cloud vertical structure (CVS) plays a fundamental role in regulating the Earth's radiation budget and hydrological cycle, yet its representation in numerical weather prediction and climate models remains highly uncertain, largely due to limited high-resolution regional observations. Using a newly established national network of 80 Ka-band millimeter-wave cloud radars (MMCRs), here we present a high-spatiotemporal-resolution (vertical resolution of 30 m, temporal resolution of 1 min) characterization of CVS across China based on one year (2024) of observations, and quantify its thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls. Cloud boundaries are retrieved using an improved algorithm that integrates height-dependent radar sensitivity with variance-based clutter suppression. Results show that the national annual mean cloud occurrence frequency is 56.7 ± 7.2 %, dominated by single-layer clouds (34.7 ± 4.0 %), followed by two-layer (14.7 ± 3.2 %) and multi-layer clouds (7.1 ± 2.4 %). Spatially, single-layer clouds prevail over arid northwestern China, whereas multi-layer clouds are more frequent in humid southeastern region. Cloud base height (CBH) exhibits strong seasonality (summer > spring > autumn > winter), with notably low CBH over the Tibetan Plateau. Diurnally, summer clouds show a pronounced afternoon peak between 3 and 9 km, while winter clouds remain largely below 3 km and peak near sunrise. Thermodynamic conditions exert the primary control on CVS. Higher 2 m specific humidity promotes deeper cloud development and raises cloud top height (CTH), whereas enhanced lower-tropospheric stability suppresses vertical cloud growth and lowers both CBH and CTH. Dynamical forcing further modulates cloud structure: stronger vertical wind shear (VWS) generally inhibits vertical cloud development, reducing CBH, CTH and cloud thickness, while moderate VWS can enhance organization under unstable conditions. Joint dependence analyses reveal that moisture, stability, and shear act in a coupled manner, with moisture being the dominant driver and stability and shear serving as strong regulators. In addition, land-surface characteristics significantly influence CBH, especially for afternoon single-layer low clouds, which exhibit a mean CBH is 21.7 % higher than the all-hour low clouds, with the strongest enhancement over evergreen broadleaf forests (+41.7 %). These findings provide the first observationally constrained, national-scale assessment of CVS based on this radar network, offering quantitative benchmarks for evaluating and improving cloud parameterizations in weather and climate models.

explanation: 该论文研究了雷击NOx的产生，使用了卫星（Meteosat 12 LI, TROPOMI）和地面（LMA）数据，涉及大气成分分析和污染物监测，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
topic_words: ['NOx', 'Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Lightning Imaging (LI)', 'TROPOMI', 'Lightning Mapping Array (LMA)']
authors: Francisco J. Pérez-Invernón;Francisco J. Gordillo-Vázquez;Oscar van der Velde;Joan Montanyà;Jesús Alberto López Trujillo;Nicolau Pineda;Diego Loyola;Sora Seo;Christoph Knote;Alexandre O. Fierro;Heidi Huntrieser
title: Characterizing lightning NOx production in the Ebro Valley with meteosat 12 LI and LMA observations
abstract:
Lightning is a major source of atmospheric pollutants. This study uses advanced satellite and ground-based data to show how lightning characteristics, such as length, brightness, and duration, affect the production of these pollutants in storms over Spain’s Ebro Valley. 
 Lightning is one of the main sources of NOx in the Earth's atmosphere, yet there is considerable variability in NOx production during thunderstorms. In this study, we combined optical lightning data from the Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Lightning Imaging (LI) instrument, which provides information on the occurrence rate and physical characteristics of lightning flashes, measurements from an extended Lightning Mapping Array (LMA) consisting of 24 sensors, lightning measurements from the Lightning Location System (LLS) of the Meteorological Service of Catalonia (MSC), and TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) cloud and NO2 research products to investigate lightning NOx emissions in the Ebro Valley (Spain). WRF-Chem simulations were used to calculate the necessary air mass factors and to subtract the NOx not produced by lightning from the TROPOMI measurements, allowing a more accurate estimation of lightning-induced NOx. We found positive relationships between lightning-produced NOx per flash and several lightning properties, including flash channel length, radiance, footprint, duration and the length of the optical continuous signal detected from space. These results highlight the importance of combining detailed lightning observations with atmospheric modeling to quantify NOx emissions from thunderstorms.

explanation: 该研究涉及大气中气体和气溶胶相的水溶性有机氮（WSON）的测量和分析，重点关注成都冬季城市大气中的污染形成机制。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，特别是空气质量监测和大气成分分析。
topic_words: ['water-soluble organic nitrogen', 'aerosol phase', 'urban atmosphere', 'air quality monitoring', 'atmospheric composition']
authors: Kaitao Chen;Zheng Li;Rui Li;Luyao Chen;Rongjie Li;Binyu Xiao;Shaojun Lv;Can Wu;Rui Li;Junke Zhang;Gehui Wang
title: Simultaneous measurements of gas- and aerosol-phase water-soluble organic nitrogen in the winter  urban atmosphere of Chengdu, China
abstract:
During winter haze in Chengdu, water-soluble organic nitrogen compounds shift from gas to particles, with concentrations more than doubling. The main driver is particle water content, not acidity or temperature. As particles absorb water, they take up these compounds, fueling aerosol growth. This study reveals how nitrogen-rich organic aerosols form in humid air, aiding pollution control strategies. 
 Partitioning gaseous water-soluble organic nitrogen (WSON) to the aerosol phase is a major formation pathway of atmospheric secondary organic aerosols (SOA). However, the factors influencing this WSON partitioning process remain unclear. We conducted simultaneous wintertime measurements of WSON in both gas and aerosol phases at an urban site in Chengdu (CD), located in the Sichuan Basin (SCB), China, to investigate the concentration, gas-particle partitioning processes, and driven factors of WSON. The average concentration of particulate WSON (2.3±1.4µgNm-3) was about twice that of gaseous WSON (1.2±0.9µgNm-3) and increased significantly as PM2.5 increased. In winter, WSON readily partitions into the particle phase (FWSON=0.70±0.14), partitioning into the organic phase under warm, dry conditions and into aerosol liquid water under cold, humid conditions, with higher FWSON in the latter. Amines (methylamine, MA; dimethylamine, DMA) were predominantly present in the gas phase but exhibited enhanced partitioning into the particle phase during the PM2.5 polluted periods. Amines preferentially partitioned into aerosol liquid water throughout the entire campaign, stably existing as amine-sulfate or amine-nitrate salts in PM2.5. The influence of aerosol liquid water content (ALWC) on the partitioning behavior of both WSON and amines was substantially greater than that of temperature (T), relative humidity (RH), and aerosol acidity (pH), as further confirmed by thermodynamic modeling with S-curve analysis. Furthermore, NH4NO3 was identified as the primary contributor to ALWC, suggesting that controlling NOx and NH3 emissions is crucial for reducing ALWC and subsequent WSON formation.

explanation: 该论文研究的是中国东部平原的暖锋暴雨现象，涉及使用雨量计和风雷达数据进行观测和分析，探讨了暴雨的识别、特征和前兆动力学信号。这些研究内容与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，特别是空气质量和大气成分分析、风场观测等方面，因此与题目要求的领域高度相关。
authors: Weilong Deng;Jianping Guo;Ning Li;Zhen Zhang;Yifei Wang;Yi Yang
title: Warm-sector heavy rainfall over the eastern China plains: identification, characteristics, and precursor dynamic signals
abstract:
Heavy rain far ahead of weather fronts is easily overlooked and hard to forecast. Using five warm seasons of rain gauge and wind radar data from eastern China's plains, we found that these brief, intense events supplied nearly half of heavy rainfall at some sites. Before rain began, fast winds at low heights became more common and the strongest upward air movements intensified. These changes could help identify warning signs, but their ability to predict individual downpours still needs testing. 
 Warm-sector heavy rainfall (WSHR) poses forecasting challenges, while its contribution to regional heavy rainfall and short-term precursors remain poorly quantified. Drawing on 2021–2025 warm-season (June–September) observations from 493 surface rain gauges, ERA5 reanalysis, and a radar wind profiler (RWP) mesonet across the eastern China plains, we build an objective identification framework integrating automated front detection, warm-sector mask, and station-specific 99th-percentile hourly rainfall thresholds to separate WSHR from other heavy rain events. We detect 477 station-based WSHR events alongside 6002 other heavy rainfall events. WSHR is spatially scattered, peaks in July–August, and preferentially begins at 20:00–03:00 Beijing Time (BJT). Accounting for merely 5 %–10 % of annual heavy rainfall occurrences, WSHR has shorter durations yet comparable median rainfall accumulations and heavier extreme rainfall tails. Among the 297 stations recording at least one WSHR event, the mean station-level contribution of WSHR to heavy-rainfall accumulation is 13.8 %, with a maximum of 48.1 %. Composite ERA5 fields show that WSHR initiates within an 850 hPa moist tongue of high pseudo-equivalent potential temperature south of the front, superimposed on strengthening low-level moisture flux convergence. RWP composites of 62 WSHR events show increasing low-level jet (LLJ) occurrence and enhanced low-level ascent shortly before rainfall onset. Comparison with 271 warm-sector non-heavy rainfall events indicates a more pronounced late increase in LLJ occurrence and a stronger upper tail of ascent speeds at 1–2 km in WSHR, although the distributions overlap substantially. These observations identify candidate kinematic indicators whose event-level predictive skill remains to be evaluated.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它的研究重点是利用中红外 limb 发射遥测技术来监测平流层气溶胶注射（SAI）的地理工程，这是一种涉及大气成分分析和卫星观测的遥感技术应用。
topic_words: ['stratospheric aerosol injection', 'mid-infrared limb emission sounding', 'satellite mission concept', 'SO2', 'sulphate aerosols']
authors: Pasquale Sellitto;Mona Kosary;Michael Höpfner;Bernd Funke;Alex Hoffmann;Jörn Ungermann;Quentin Errera;Simone Tilmes;Björn-Martin Sinnhuber
title: The enhanced capabilities of mid-infrared limb emission sounding to observe stratospheric aerosol injection geoengineering
abstract:
To counterbalance human-caused global warming, highly controversial geoengineering techniques, based on stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI), have been proposed as a complement to climate change mitigation. Possible unilateral SAI deployments or tests are a risk. We show that existing satellite instruments do not have the capability to detect unilateral SAI experiments and we propose a future satellite technique, infrared limb emission sounding, that can provide this missing capability. 
 Using a model-based pseudo-reality (PR) future scenario and realistic pseudo-observations (POs) representative for a proposed satellite mission concept (CAIRT – the Changing-Atmosphere Infra-Red Tomography explorer), we analyse the capabilities of a high-spectral-resolution limb-emission sounding technique to detect and quantitatively monitor very weak stratospheric aerosol injections (SAI) geoengineering deployments, in terms of the injected sulphur dioxide (SO2) and its evolution into sulphate aerosols (SA). Our results suggest that this technique would detect SO2 injections, at the horizontal and vertical scale, within hours to a few days since the SAI deployment. This concept would quantify the SO2 injected mass, even for injections of the order of magnitude of a few hundreds of tonnes of SO2 per day, characteristic of “near-term” to “mid-term” experiments feasible even unilaterally, or in the context of small-scale outdoor experiments, with presently existing technology and at relatively low cost. In addition, our results suggest that this concept would be able to track the temporal evolution of the subsequently formed SA, as it spreads zonally and then toward higher latitudes through meridional dispersion, and to monitor changes in its vertical distribution over time through processes like self-lofting of the resulting SA plume. Existing satellite instruments, e.g. based on limb scattering, solar occultation, nadir observations and space LiDARs, do not have the capability to carry out such strategical observations of SAI. Our results stress the importance of increasing our global observational capabilities with high-spectral-resolution limb-emission satellite instruments, a capability not available at present and not foreseen in the near future.

topic_words: ['satellite microwave links', 'precipitation monitoring', 'rain gauges', 'weather radars', 'atmospheric composition analysis']
authors: Roberto Nebuloni;Maximilian Graf;Greta Cazzaniga;François Mercier;Maxime Turko
title: The OpenSat4Weather dataset: Ku-band satellite link data for precipitation monitoring
abstract:
We describe the OpenSat4Weather public dataset, which provides time series of received power from 215 TV-SAT satellite microwave links located in Southern France over a five-month observation period and at 1-min resolution. These data can be processed to gather indirect rainfall intensity measurements. OpenSat4Weather also includes concurrent data from operational rain gauges and weather radars, and ERA5 0°C isotherm height data, to derive the wet fraction of the satellite-to-ground path. 
 The TV-SAT signals received by the ground antennas of Satellite Microwave Links (SMLs) can be opportunistically used for detecting and quantifying precipitation. Consequently, SMLs have the potential to serve as low-cost rainfall sensors complementing conventional instruments. However,  a major challenge for opportunistic sensors, including both SMLs and their terrestrial counterpart – Commercial Microwave Links (CMLs) – is related to data ownership and accessibility  constraints, possibly hindering progress in the development of processing tools and validation studies. This limitation highlights the importance  of openly accessible datasets. While CML open datasets are already available, there are no large-scale SML datasets in public repositories. To address  this gap, we introduce  the OpenSat4Weather dataset, a comprehensive and openly accessible collection of measurements  from 215 SML sensors deployed in Southern France, over a five-month period from August to December 2022. The dataset is accessible at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16530166 (Nebuloni et al., 2025b). OpenSat4Weather also includes concurrent conventional measurements, namely, 6 min rainfall depths from 113 operational rain gauges, and radar-based estimates of rainfall intensity along each SML path. The radar data were derived from the gauge-adjusted weather radar product PANTHERE provided by Météo-France. Additionally, the dataset stores ERA5 reanalysis data of the 0 °C isotherm height for rain height estimation, which are essential for accurately converting the  received signal level into rainfall intensity.In this paper, we detail the OpenSat4Weather data preparation process and draw statistics of data availability. We then  provide a descriptive analysis of the dataset, including  rainfall characteristics, derived from rain gauges,  statistical properties of the SML received signal levels, and a comparison between SML and radar data. In addition, we illustrate  examples of disturbances and anomalous patterns observed in raw SML signals. Finally, we provide some practical guidelines for processing and analyzing SML data. Our ultimate goal is to promote open research initiatives aimed at accelerating the development of SML-based applications. Enhancing rainfall monitoring  by opportunistic sensors has the potential to provide  substantial benefits, particularly   in regions where conventional networks are  sparse or unavailable.

title: Atlas of geochemical, petrophysical and mechanical rock properties of the crystalline basement in Germany – first release
abstract:
The AMPEDEK database is the first standardized, open-access database of rock properties for Germany's crystalline basement. By combining published data with new laboratory measurements, it provides 25,700 petrophysical and mechanical data points, as well as geochemical and mineralogical data, from more than 8,200 samples collected across eight federal states. The database supports preliminary reservoir assessments and future exploration campaigns for a wide range of geological applications. 
 A comprehensive and statistically robust understanding of rock characteristics is essential for reservoir characterization of the deep subsurface to accurately plan exploration campaigns, parameterize predictive 3D geological models, interpret geophysical data, and execute numerical thermo-hydraulic-mechanical-chemical simulations, thereby reducing economic risks and project uncertainties. Despite growing interest in the crystalline basement in Germany for e.g., geothermal energy applications and the safe storage of high-radioactive nuclear waste, systematic datasets covering the major crystalline and metamorphic basement units and their physiomechanical characteristics remain scarce, fragmented, or lack the metadata required for robust evaluation. To address this data gap, the AMPEDEK project established a unified, multi-scale national reference database for geochemical, petrophysical, and mechanical rock properties of crystalline rocks in Germany. The framework integrated extensive literature reviews, data from geological surveys, and newly conducted sampling and measurement campaigns, linking metadata, geochemistry, petrography, and physiomechanical rock properties through unique sample IDs.

title: marinedb: An open-source, flexible and scalable Python workflow for curating, standardizing, and integrating marine biodiversity data
abstract:
Knowing where marine species live helps us understand and protect ocean life, but the underlying records are spread across sources, vary widely in how they were collected, described, and formatted, and are affected by data-quality issues. We developed marinedb, an open tool for cleaning biodiversity data, and used it to build a global dataset of nearly 159 million records covering more than 139,000 species, making large-scale studies of marine species distributions easier and more reproducible. 
 The digital era and the emergence of data-aggregation initiatives have greatly expanded access to biodiversity occurrence records, but accessibility alone does not ensure usability for ecological modeling. Marine occurrence data must be cleaned and reconciled across spatial, temporal, and taxonomic dimensions before they can be reliably linked to environmental predictors and used to model species distributions. Here, we introduce marinedb, an open-source, modular, and scalable Python package for curating marine occurrence data. The package provides a suite of tools that can be freely combined into user-defined workflows tailored to study objectives and data characteristics. We applied marinedb to three major biodiversity resources: the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), the Ocean Biogeographic Information System (OBIS), and the Jellyfish Database Initiative (JeDI). Together, these resources span hundreds of millions of occurrence records located at sea and more than one hundred thousand species. First, we used the framework to assess data quality non-destructively across the three sources. The analysis revealed substantial and source-dependent issues, including records located on land, missing depth information, heterogeneous, incomplete, or low-precision temporal information, records lacking species-level information or referring to non-marine taxa, weak or unspecified evidential support, absence records, and strong taxonomic imbalance. Second, we applied a tailored dataset-production workflow to produce a ready-to-use global marine occurrence dataset for large-scale modeling of present-day species distributions, which comprises 158,910,536 records representing 139,844 species. Together, the reusable Python tools and the curated dataset derived from GBIF, OBIS, and JeDI lower the technical barrier for multi-species and deep-learning approaches, both of which require extensive and diverse occurrence records, while preserving flexibility for future use-case-specific curation.

title: A High-Resolution Gridded Dataset of Vertically Resolved Fine Root Biomass Across China
abstract:
Fine roots help plants take up water and nutrients and store carbon in soil. We developed a dataset showing the vertical distribution of fine roots across China from 2005–2025. Using thousands of field measurements and environmental data, we mapped root biomass in 20 cm layers down to 2 m. The dataset reveals strong differences in root distribution among regions and plant types and provides a new resource for understanding belowground carbon storage and ecosystem change. 
 Fine root plays a critical role in ecosystem biogeochemical cycles, serving as the primary organs for water and nutrient uptake and exhibiting rapid turnover. However, a spatially explicit dataset of fine root biomass (FRB) across soil profiles and vegetation types remains lacking. To address this knowledge gap, we compiled 2,311 in-situ measurements of woody FRB and 3,580 measurements of herbaceous FRB from peer-reviewed studies across China. Using these observations, we developed random forest models to estimate surface-layer (0–20 cm) FRB and the vertical attenuation coefficient (k) of FRB for woody and herbaceous ecosystems, respectively. By integrating the predicted surface-layer FRB and vertical distribution functions, we finally generated a gridded dataset of FRB across 0–2 m soil depth (at 20 cm intervals) at 1 km spatial resolution for all woody and herbaceous ecosystems in China for 2005–2025. Model evaluation showed that our models explain approximately 86 % and 81 % of the observed variations in surface FRB across woody and herbaceous ecosystems, respectively, and reasonablely capture the interannual dynamics of observed FRB. Model predictions reveal substantial spatial and vertical variations in both woody and herbaceous FRB across China. Woody FRB density was generally higher in southern China than in central and northern China, whereas herbaceous FRB density was highest on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Woody plants exhibit deeper root distributions in arid regions, whereas herbaceous species show consistently surface-concentrated rooting patterns across climate zones. The environmental controls of FRB also differed between vegetation types, with woody FRB being more strongly influenced by root traits and nutrient availability, whereas herbaceous FRB was more closely associated with climatic conditions. This dataset provides an observation-constrained, spatially explicit benchmark for quantifying belowground carbon stocks and dynamics, and it is archived and publicly available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32353257 (Zheng et al., 2026).

authors: Victor J. H. Trees;Ping Wang;Job I. Wiltink;Piet Stammes;Daphne M. Stam;David P. Donovan;A. Pier Siebesma
title: MONKI: a three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulator for transfer of polarised light in planetary atmospheres
abstract:
We present MONKI (Monte Carlo KNMI), an accurate and efficient Fortran radiative transfer code for simulating total and polarised sunlight in 3D planetary atmospheres. Its novelty is the derivation of Monte Carlo equations for the transfer of polarised light, fully accounting for polarisation-dependent scattering directions. This formulation gives reliable convergence even for optically thick, strongly polarising atmospheres, supporting observations of Earth, Venus, or any other planet. 
 Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool for characterising planetary atmospheres and surfaces. For the design and operation of spectro(polari)metric instrumentation, numerically simulated signals of the measured radiation are essential. We present MONKI (Monte Carlo KNMI), an efficient and accurate Monte Carlo radiative transfer code written in Fortran. MONKI computes total, linearly polarised, and circularly polarised radiances reflected by and transmitted through planetary atmospheres, fully accounting for the polarisation of light in all orders of scattering. Unlike classical Monte Carlo approaches that rely on post-sampling weight corrections and can therefore produce rare but disproportionately large photon weights, MONKI samples scattering directions from the full polarisation-dependent distribution, consistently in both forward and backward Monte Carlo modes. We provide the corresponding theoretical framework in the appendices. Because of this exact polarised sampling approach, the code converges robustly for optically thick and/or strongly polarising atmospheres. MONKI can handle horizontally homogeneous atmospheres as well as atmospheres with horizontal inhomogeneities, such as three-dimensional (3D) patchy clouds. We validate MONKI through comparisons with other radiative transfer codes. Finally, we present sample simulations of sunlight reflected by the Earth and Venus, and explain the total and polarised radiance features by analysing the altitudes at which photons are scattered. We conclude that MONKI is a versatile and accurate tool for simulations and detailed analyses of total and polarised light emerging from the atmospheres of the Earth, Venus, and, in principle, any other planet.

authors: Ross N. Bannister
title: EnviFlux (v1.0): a simplified surface flux inversion tool based on four-dimensional variational data assimilation (4D-Var)
abstract:
EnviFlux is described, and then used to show how model error and bias can influence the inferred surface flux features. This is done in two scenarios, one with no prior knowledge of a source/sink pair, and another with prior knowledge in a more realistic situation. 
 This paper introduces EnviFlux, which is a software tool (written in C++) to study the inverse problem of estimating the distribution of fluxes of a trace gas globally at the Earth's surface. This is done using a four-dimensional variational technique, which combines information from (i) synthetic observations of the trace gas spanning a defined time window, (ii) a transport model linking the initial concentration and surface fluxes to predictions of the observations, and (iii) a priori information. The novelty of this system – compared to those that attempt to solve for real data – is in its relative simplicity and low cost, allowing new ideas to be assessed and understood quickly and cheaply. This is in line with many other developments in data assimilation that are often first explored using so-called “toy” systems. Part of this paper is to document this system, which is sufficiently complex to allow assimilation of in situ and total column amount (TCA) observation in arbitrary configurations, and has a flexible background error covariance model, but is simple enough to be run relatively quickly.Another part of this paper uses EnviFlux to explore the effect of model error and observation bias on inferred surface fluxes in two example scenarios and with two observation types, namely surface in situ (SIS) and TCA. The first is a highly idealised case with a flux pair (a localised source and a localised sink), where no a priori information concerning their positions is provided. It is found that model errors in the assimilation can severely affect the inferred flux positions and amounts, but observation biases do not affect the positions, but do affect the amounts. The second scenario is closer to a real-world example of methane flux estimates where an a priori is refined with observations. The effect of model error is less than for the first scenario, but is still evident, and the observation biases affect the flux amounts. In both cases, the SIS observations allow a more accurate estimate of surface flux characteristics than the TCA observations, even though the experiments are setup to allow a fair comparison of the two. The last part of the paper raises some research questions that EnviFlux could help address.

title: Improving the CLASSIC (v1.8) snow model  to better simulate Arctic snowpacks
abstract:
This study enhances a snow model for Arctic environments by improving the heat exchanges within the snowpack and at its interfaces, revising the compaction scheme, and adding consideration of blowing snow sublimation losses. Simulations at ten Arctic, mid-latitude, and Alpine sites show significant reductions in simulated soil and snow temperature biases and improved simulated snow depth and density, which are key features to improve simulated energy, water, and carbon budgets in the Arctic. 
 This study enhances the snow model of the Canadian Land Surface Scheme including Biogeochemical Cycles (CLASSIC), with a particular focus on Arctic environments. Key snow model physics improvements include adjustments to the thermal conductivity at the top of the first soil layer, a revised computation of the temperature at the snow–soil interface (hereafter, bottom snow temperature), and the addition of a windless exchange coefficient in sensible heat flux calculations. Arctic-specific adaptations include blowing-snow sublimation losses, a new snow compaction scheme, and snow thermal conductivity parameterization. Evaluations at seven mid-latitude and alpine sites (SnowMIP sites) and three Arctic sites (Bylot Island, Umiujaq, and Trail Valley Creek) show that these enhancements improve the overall simulated snowpack characteristics and soil temperatures across both SnowMIP and Arctic sites. The revised bottom snow temperature yields better agreement between simulated and observed snow and bottom snow temperatures. The new windless exchange coefficient reduced the surface temperature RMSE from 3.50 to 1.93 °C on average across all sites. The improved snow compaction scheme reduces the snow depth biases from 12.0 to 0.1 cm on average across the Arctic sites and improves the simulated snow densities while not degrading the overall model performance at the SnowMIP sites. Blowing-snow sublimation had a negligible effect at most sites, except at the wind-exposed sites of Umiujaq, Trail Valley Creek, and Senator Beck, decreasing snow depth on average by 2–4 cm. Adding a new snow thermal conductivity parameterization – combined with all previous developments – reduces the RMSE of the simulated soil temperatures from 5.3 to 3.0 °C on average at all Arctic sites. Our new developments demonstrate the ability of a single-layer snow model to reasonably reproduce Arctic bulk snowpack characteristics, while maintaining good performance at the SnowMIP sites. Inherent uncertainties remain in the forcing datasets, especially due to the harsh Arctic environment characterized by strong winds, snow redistribution, frost, and polar night. Future model developments will focus on spatial-scale simulations across the whole Arctic, with particular attention to snow cover fraction parameterizations to better capture sub-grid-scale spatial heterogeneity in Arctic environments.

title: Process-based evaluation of green roof models for assessment of heat mitigation efficacy in WRF (v4.3.1) and EnergyPlus (v8.6.0)
abstract:
Green roofs can help cool cities, but models must represent them accurately to quantify this potential. Yet few studies evaluate green roof models against real data. We evaluated two versions of EcoRoof, the green roof module in EnergyPlus, and a green roof option for WRF (Weather and Research Forecasting model) using measurements from London, Ontario. EcoRoof generally matched observed heat fluxes, surface temperature, and soil moisture, while WRF overestimated heat and underestimated cooling. 
 Green roofs mitigate urban heat, but to fully assess their impact, green roof models must be integrated into urban climate models, where they provide critical surface boundary conditions. Ensuring their reliability requires evaluation, yet such efforts remain limited in the literature. This study addresses that gap by evaluating two configurations of EcoRoof, the green roof module from EnergyPlus (ERo for the original version of the model, and ERm for a modified version), and a multilayer green roof parametrization for WRF (WRF-MLGR) (Heusinger et al., 2018; Sailor, 2008; Zonato et al., 2021). These models were tested against field observations from a monitored green roof in London, Ontario, focusing on latent heat flux (Qe), surface temperature (Tsurf), soil heat flux (Qg) and substrate water content (SWC). Model performance varied by variable. The two EcoRoof versions showed similar performance, with mean RMSE across study periods of approximately 56–60 W m−2 for Qe, 3–4 °C for Tsurf, 22 W m−2 for Qg, and 0.03 m3 m−3 for SWC. Performance for Qe was comparable across models; however, WRF-MLGR exhibited much larger errors for Qg (with mean RMSE exceeding 100 W m−2) and SWC (0.06 m3 m−3), along with higher Tsurf deviations (∼5 °C). Overall, EcoRoof provided a more consistent representation of the daytime energy balance, whereas WRF-MLGR showed structural biases in surface heating. These findings highlight the importance of process-level evaluation for urban climate applications and underscore the need for continued model development to address the structural limitations in green roof parametrizations.

title: Towards high-fidelity simulations of coastal submesoscale  baroclinic instabilities with MPAS–O (vE3SM3.0.0)  – Part 2: Realistic experiments
abstract:
River plumes can strongly influence coastal dynamics but are poorly resolved in global ocean models. Building on a companion study, we perform high-resolution simulations of the Mississippi–Atchafalaya (M–A) plume with the Model for Prediction Across Scales–Ocean (MPAS–O), a global model, and compare with a limited-domain Regional Ocean Modeling System configuration. MPAS–O qualitatively captures the M–A plume seasonality but fails to generate realistic eddies on the Texas–Louisiana shelf. 
 River plumes can strongly influence coastal dynamics but are poorly represented in global ocean models due to stringent resolution requirements. Following the idealized simulations presented in a companion paper (Hinson et al., 2026), this study presents submesoscale-permitting realistic simulations using unprecedented regional refinement with MPAS–O. We assess MPAS–O's ability to represent river plume dynamics by comparing with a validated ROMS configuration focused on the Mississippi–Atchafalaya (M–A) plume in the northern Gulf of Mexico (GoM). The variable-resolution mesh spans 1.4 km in the GoM to 100 km in the Pacific and Indian Oceans. We incorporate several improvements to the representation of river forcing in MPAS–O: the pseudo point source treatment of runoff, river temperature prescribed from air temperature, and passive tracers to track freshwater transport. MPAS–O generates vigorous submesoscales in the open GoM, as quantified by probability density functions of surface relative vorticity and divergence. While the model qualitatively captures the M–A plume's seasonal evolution, it does not realistically reproduce the summer submesoscale eddy field on the Texas–Louisiana shelf. A persistent brackish lens associated with reduced vertical mixing forms and is present throughout the M–A plume. We hypothesize that this arises from interacting parameterization and structural design choices within MPAS–O that affect plume stratification and instability growth under realistic forcing, rather than from deficiencies in numerics. Our results demonstrate MPAS–O's potential for simulating submesoscale processes in the open ocean while highlighting challenges in using regional refinement to model coastal dynamics.

title: Evaluating the EPICC-Model for regional air quality simulation: a comparative study with CAMx and CMAQ
abstract:
This study compares the model performance of the Emission and atmospheric Processes Integrated and Coupled Community Model with the two air quality models in China. The EPICC-Model excels in simulating summer ozone peaks, accurately captures pollution characteristics in highly polluted areas, and better reproduces persistent compound pollution processes. The study reveals common issues among the models and directions for improvement, providing a basis for optimizing global air quality models. 
 This study presents a systematic evaluation of the EPICC-Model developed in China for regional PM2.5 and MDA8 O3 simulations against established international models, using WRF meteorological fields and a multi-source integrated emission inventory. Results highlight the strengths of the EPICC-Model in several aspects: it achieves relatively high spatial consistency with measurements for PM2.5, with an annual index of agreement (IOA) of 0.80, and accurately captures pollution patterns in heavily polluted North China. It also demonstrates improved performance in simulating summer O3 peaks, reducing maximum bias by more than 20 µg m−3; this performance may be partly associated with its inclusion of heterogeneous HONO formation and particulate nitrate photolysis. The model exhibits the highest hit rate (45.6 %) for MDA8 O3 pollution events exceeding 160 µg m−3 and successfully reproduces persistent pollution episodes. However, all models share common limitations, including insufficient capability in reproducing heavy pollution episodes, systematic underestimation of SO42-, and uncertainties in SOA-related OC simulations. Future improvements should focus on refining secondary aerosol chemistry and emission inventories and further evaluating the representation of vertical turbulent mixing under stable boundary-layer conditions. This study benchmarks the performance of the EPICC-Model against established chemical transport models (CTMs) and identifies priorities for its further development and regional application.

title: Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria
abstract:
Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria 
 Defense-associated reverse transcriptases (DRTs) employ diverse and distinctive mechanisms of cDNA synthesis to protect bacteria against viral infection1. However, the functions and mechanisms of many DRTs remain unknown2. Here we identify a new antiviral defense system, DRT10, that associates with a noncoding RNA (ncRNA) to catalyze processive, protein-primed synthesis of tandem-repeat DNA. Reverse transcription is templated by a defined ncRNA region with a characteristic sequence pattern and template boundary elements, both of which are conserved and essential for DNA repeat addition. Cryo-EM reconstructions reveal an unanticipated 2:1 architecture, wherein two RT monomers bind opposite sides of a pseudo-symmetric ncRNA. Biochemical experiments further demonstrate that each RT monomer reverse transcribes the template encoded on its respective side of the ncRNA, but only one generates the long repetitive product, whose template is defined by the distance between two flanking stem-loop anchors. This mode of iterative, boundary-delimited cDNA synthesis exhibits direct parallels to the mechanism of telomeric repeat addition by eukaryotic telomerase, and phylogenetic analyses of RTs across domains of life place telomerase in a monophyletic clade with the DRT family, suggesting a common origin for their DNA polymerization activities. Together with earlier studies of DRT2, DRT3, and DRT93–5, our findings identify a conserved mechanistic logic underlying RNA-templated DNA repeat addition across diverse DRTs, despite vastly different architectural solutions, and expand the repertoire of reverse transcription-based strategies for antiviral immunity in bacteria.

title: An abrupt shift towards a hotter and drier climate regime in the Western Eurasian Steppe
abstract:
The Western Eurasian Steppe has undergone an abrupt and persistent transition to a hotter and drier summer climate that exceeds the range of natural variability, driven by external climate forcing and amplified by internal variability and land–atmosphere feedbacks, according to observations and Earth system model simulations. 
 Semiarid drylands, with their strong land–atmosphere coupling, are increasingly recognized as highly sensitive to anthropogenic forcing. Yet whether this sensitivity can give rise to abrupt hydroclimatic transitions under sustained warming remains unclear. Here, using reanalysis data and large-ensemble and multi-model climate simulations, we identify an abrupt climate regime shift in the Western Eurasian Steppe, marked by unprecedented summer drying that exceeds the range of natural variability over the past century. This drying transition shows no clear sign of recovery during the observational period (1901–2024). External forcing provided the background drying, while internal climate variability amplified the regional trend since the early 1990s. Declining soil moisture weakens evaporative cooling and strengthens sensible heat flux, intensifying heat extremes and deepening hydrological deficits. This intensified land–atmosphere feedback has amplified drying and heat extremes to unprecedented levels over the past six decades, contributing to widespread land degradation and reduced gross primary productivity. The Western Eurasian Steppe thus serves as an early warning signal for other Northern Hemisphere mid-latitude drylands, where similar land–atmosphere feedbacks may also promote abrupt and persistent regime shifts under continued warming. title: Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation
abstract:
Mitigating errors in analogue quantum simulators - that is, reducing noise-induced bias in expectation values - would greatly improve their operation and scalability. Here, the authors propose a time-continuous error cancellation protocol, based on introducing an auxiliary system and engineering the joint dissipation of the new, extended system. 
 Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise. title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
abstract:
Origin-destination data on air travel are essential for studying global mobility and epidemic risk but are often proprietary. Here, authors introduce a maximum-entropy network method that reconstructs air passenger flows from open data and enables accurate reproduction of epidemic dynamics. 
 Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems. title: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex
abstract:
Neural mechanisms underlying one-shot memory are not fully understood. In this study, macaque monkeys were trained to perform a continuous image recognition task and simultaneously recorded from groups of neurons in area V4. The authors found that the perceptual building blocks of fast, high-capacity memory are present in mid-level sensory cortex. 
 High-capacity, one-shot visual recognition memory challenges theories of learning and neural coding because it requires rapid, robust, and durable representations. Most studies have focused on the hippocampus and other higher areas. However, behavioral evidence demonstrating links between image properties and memorability and revealing image specificity of visual memory suggests an important role for mid-level visual cortex. We tested the hypothesis that area V4 contains signals critical for recognition memory in two male rhesus macaques. Our task increased difficulty, allowing comparisons of neuronal population responses on correct and error trials. We observed signatures of several proposed memory mechanisms including magnitude coding, repetition suppression, sparse coding, and population response consistency, but only sparse coding and population response consistency predicted behavior. Familiar images also evoked faster dynamics, consistent with pattern completion. These findings demonstrate that fast, high-capacity memory is supported by neural codes in mid-level sensory cortex independent of stimulus features per se, highlighting its role in distributed memory networks. title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54<sup>+</sup>/iNOS<sup>+</sup> neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis
abstract:
Neutrophils have been shown to be involved in pulmonary fibrosis (PF). Here, the authors identify an expanded pro-inflammatory neutrophil state marked by CD54 in human PF and by iNOS in murine PF, demonstrate that iNOS+ neutrophils promote PF whilst Arg+ neutrophils are less effective, and show that mechanical activation of the PIEZO1 channel contributes to the promotion of PF by CD54 + /iNOS+ neutrophils. 
 Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54+ neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS+ neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS+ neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS+ neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils. title: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract:
Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity. 
 Tau propagation is a key driver of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet selective markers of seeding-competent tau remain elusive. Ubiquitin phosphorylated at Serine-65 (pS65-Ub) is a PINK1-derived cellular stress signal that accumulates in AD with elevated tau pathology, but its relationship to tau seeding is unknown. Here, using postmortem brain tissue from female and male donors, we show that a subset of tau is covalently modified by pS65-Ub in AD brain. The pS65-Ub-associated tau population is elevated in AD and is enriched in soluble, high-molecular-weight, oligomeric, and hyperphosphorylated tau species. Across AD cases, soluble pS65-Ub-associated tau levels strongly correlate with tau seeding activity. Tau species isolated with pS65-Ub antibodies exhibit seeding activity, whereas removal of pS65-Ub-associated material markedly reduces seeding from AD brain extracts. Together, these findings identify pS65-Ub as a disease-enriched molecular feature of a seed-competent tau population and link cellular stress signaling with pathological tau propagation in AD. Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity.

title: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
abstract:
Ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical. Here, the authors integrate interpretable machine learning with modular degradable lipid chemistry to prioritize candidates for experimental testing and identify a lead lipid for hepatic mRNA delivery. 
 Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery. title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
abstract:
What is the mechanism by which ClpXP utilizes ATP to unfold proteins? Using single-molecule, biochemical and structural methods, the authors find that the central coupler facilitates the conversion of chemical energy into a quick motion of substrate translocating loops to generate force. 
 ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor. Using single-molecule, biochemical and structural methods, the authors find that the central coupler facilitates the conversion of chemical energy into a quick motion of substrate translocating loops to generate force.

title: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction
abstract:
Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan. 
 Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. Agreement between model predictions and observations supports the hypothesis that observed slip diversity, including fast earthquakes and slow transient slips (Slow Slip Events; SSEs), originates from frictional heterogeneity. However, quantitative assessments of frictional heterogeneity from geodetic observations while fully incorporating fault mechanics are lacking due to the difficulties of high-dimensional optimization. In this study, we aim to address this gap using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to link frictional heterogeneity with geodetic observations. PINNs employ a neural network to represent the spatially variable frictional properties, making their estimation feasible. Targeting the 2010 Bungo SSE in southwest Japan, our estimation reveals heterogeneous friction coinciding with localized SSE nucleation in southwest Shikoku, and subsequent westward propagation. The calculated fault slip of SSE successfully reproduces the spatio-temporal pattern of observed surface displacements. This PINN-based inversion provides a mechanically consistent fault slip model validated through quantitative comparison with observations. Furthermore, we forecast the future fault slip evolution, demonstrating the importance of assimilating observations spanning multiple SSE cycles. Our results demonstrate the potential of PINN for advancing understanding of fault mechanics and enabling physics-based fault slip forecasting. Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan.

title: Baltic Sea sediment bacterial communities show asymmetric and incomplete recovery after reciprocal temperature change translocation
abstract:
Ocean warming will alter bacterial communities of Baltic Sea coastal sediments and associated biogeochemical cycles, according to translocation experiments of Baltic Sea sediment. 
 Marine coastal systems are important for global biogeochemical cycling and are particularly sensitive to climate change effects due to their shallow depths, which results in rapid heat transfer to the sediments. Here we used one-year reciprocal in situ translocations of sediments between a Baltic Sea long-term (>50 years) warming-influenced bay and a nearby unaffected control bay to predict how the sediments and their associated bacterial communities may respond to future climate change and whether those changes were reversible. Geochemical parameters, methane plus sulfate profiles, and 16S rRNA gene-based bacterial diversity and community composition show partial convergence of the sediment-parameters to the translocated environment, suggesting climate change will rapidly alter bacteria communities of Baltic Sea coastal sediments. However, more pronounced responses in the control to the heated bay translocation direction suggest that while a return toward present-day conditions may be possible if climate change is reversed, such a recovery may be incomplete or require a longer time than one year. Ocean warming will alter bacterial communities of Baltic Sea coastal sediments and associated biogeochemical cycles, according to translocation experiments of Baltic Sea sediment.
